title: long-tail-phase-fuzzer-and-quantile-stability-reporter
author: Ethan Chen
description: Motivation: production latency regressions often show up as non-deterministic micro-spikes in the long tail. This PR introduces a long-tail phase fuzzer that injects controlled micro-jitter into scheduling/kv-cache warmup paths during benchmarks, plus a Quantile Stability Reporter that measures quantile drift across repeated runs and surfaces unstable kernels or scheduling regimes. The goal is to (1) expose non-deterministic p99+/p999 mode changes earlier in CI and local profiling, (2) provide a compact stability score per-kernel and per-sequence-length bucket, and (3) produce machine-readable reports for upstream alerting and triage. Changes: added a phase-based fuzzer that can run in-process or as a sidecar to benchlab-runner; implemented deterministic primer replay to warm KV caches uniformly across nodes; added sequence-length bucketer that amplifies long-tail sequences (1000+ tokens) while preserving real traffic mixes; added Quantile Stability Reporter that computes stability coefficients across N runs and outputs CSV/JSON and a concise markdown summary; wiring to benchlab CI dashboards and new alert thresholds. Testing: unit tests for deterministic primer, integration harness that runs the fuzzer against a pinned model and compares stability scores with and without jitter, and end-to-end runbook used to reproduce a flakiness incident. Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag benchlab.phase_fuzzer.enabled=false by default; gradual opt-in for nightly perf suites; CI enhanced to run a short seeded-fuzz job on release branches. Checklist: [x] design doc updated with graph examples [x] unit + integration tests [x] docs and runbook [x] benchlab-dashboard tile config [x] feature-flag gated. Related: ENG-1579 (long-tail flakiness), SUP-8412 (customer hit on p99 spikes).

feature: deterministic primer replay and cross-node coordinator
feature: quantile stability reporter and CSV/JSON exporters

docs: design doc, runbook, and dashboard tile config
fix: reduce nondeterminism in seeded RNG and address flaky test timing

review_comments: Anjali Rao: Nice isolation of primer logic — can we make the cross-node coordinator optional so smaller runners don't pay the dependency? (resolved by optional flag and lightweight local coordinator)
Marissa López: Tests look comprehensive; one nit: tighten the RNG seeding so that CI reproducibility across platforms is consistent (addressed by using HMAC-based seed derivation)
Omar Al-Hassan: Quantile Stability score calculation is sensible. Suggest we include a per-bucket sample count in the output for triage (added sample_count to JSON and CSV headers)
Ethan Chen (author): Thanks all — addressed comments, added runbook steps to reproduce locally, and gated feature behind benchlab.phase_fuzzer.enabled flag.
release_notes: Add long-tail phase fuzzer (opt-in) and Quantile Stability Reporter for detecting nondeterministic latency regressions. Feature is disabled by default and can be enabled with benchlab.phase_fuzzer.enabled=true. Produces machine-readable stability metrics consumed by perf dashboards.
notes_for_oncall: If nightly seeded-fuzz job shows sudden stability_score drop (>20% relative), the runbook under benchmark-lab/runbooks/long_tail_flakiness.md should be followed: triage kernels by bucket, reproduce with --seed=... and collect kernel traces. For urgent customer regressions, enable feature flag on a small cohort and run full kv-cache primer.
